method.route_used: help.sap.com/docs/** and learning.sap.com/courses/** are JS shells for WebFetch; every page was re-rendered independently with the in-app browser (preview_start + navigate + get_page_text) and the verbatim page text was diffed against each evidence_quote. 1-2 get_page_text retries were needed per help.sap.com page while 'Loading Topic...' resolved. Rendered page <title> was checked against the intended topic on every page to guard against the GUID-portability trap recorded in the lane's own gaps.
method.http_status_note: The browser route does not surface a numeric status code. 'verifier_http_status' is recorded as '200-RENDERED' where the intended topic rendered in full and its title matched. No page in this lane 404'd, redirected, or gated.
method.tier_note: The lane self-tiered learning.sap.com as 2-VENDOR-LEARNING. Under the verifier gate, learning.sap.com counts as Tier 1 for SAP product behaviour, so those CONFIRMED verdicts hold under either tiering. help.sap.com/docs/SUPPORT_CONTENT/spmm/3362167804.html is SAP-hosted SUPPORT WIKI content ('Additional Content'), not product documentation; the lane's conservative 2-VENDOR-LEARNING tiering is retained here. It reaches CONFIRMED only because its claims are behavioural, which Tier 2 permits.

Quote is verbatim INCLUDING its confusing arithmetic. Full worked example: PR 5 PC @ EUR 1500 = 7500 commitment. PO for 3 PC @ EUR 2000 creates a PO commitment of 6000. 'The system reduces the purchase requisition commitment in proportion to quantity to EUR 3,000.00 (3 x EUR 1,500.00 = EUR 4,500.00).' Correct reading: the PR commitment is relieved BY 4,500 (3 units x the REQUISITION price 1,500), leaving a residual balance of 3,000 (2 units x 1,500). The parenthetical is the reduction amount, not the resulting balance.
results.notes: LOAD-BEARING AND EASY TO MIS-READ. The claim ('at the requisition price, not the PO price') is exactly right and is the whole point of the example - the PO price of 2,000 never touches the PR relief. But the SAP sentence reads as self-contradictory on its face, so any downstream implementer who copies it verbatim without this gloss will get the residual wrong. Corroborated by the S/4HANA Cloud PSM lesson: 'the open amount is calculated by considering the open quantity first. This mechanism avoids open amounts in the case of price decreases.'

results.what_source_actually_says: Verbatim: 'The goods receipt indicator in the purchase order determines when the commitment is reduced and actual costs are set up (that is, in the detail screen for the purchase order item).'
results.notes: CONFIRMED AS QUOTED BUT INCOMPLETE AS A DESIGN RULE - see contradictions[0]. The GR indicator is only the FIRST of two gates. The 'goods receipt non-valuated' flag (EKPO/EKBP-WEUNB) is the second, and it can send relief to the invoice even when the GR indicator IS set. Any anti-double-count implementation keying solely on the GR indicator will mis-time relief on non-valuated-GR purchase orders.

The quoted row label exists, but the claim misreads the table. The full table on 'Example: Reducing the Purchase Order Commitment' is: (1) PO 3 PC @ USD 1500 + USD 150 freight -> Actual ./. , Commitment 4650.00, Assigned 4650.00. (2) GR for two PC -> Actual 3100.00, Commitment 1550.00, Assigned 4650.00. (3) IR for three PC @ USD 2000 each -> Actual 4100.00, Commitment 2050.00, Assigned 6150.00. (4) GR for one PC -> Actual 6150.00, Commitment ./. , Assigned 6150.00. At the invoice-receipt step ACTUAL moves 3,100.00 -> 4,100.00, NOT 4,650.00 -> 6,150.00. Only ASSIGNED moves 4,650.00 -> 6,150.00 at that step. Actual only reaches 6,150.00 at step 4, the final goods receipt.
results.notes: DOWNGRADED. NARROWER TRUE STATEMENT: an invoice priced above the PO (2,000 vs 1,500) raises the ASSIGNED total from 4,650.00 to 6,150.00; the Actual column reads 4,100.00 at that step. Do not seed test scenarios from this claim as written - the numbers will not reconcile. Two further design-relevant facts visible in the table and not captured by any record in this lane: (a) the invoice for three PC is posted while only two PC had been received, and it INCREASES commitment from 1,550.00 to 2,050.00 rather than reducing it - a price/quantity revaluation, not a relief; (b) Assigned is flat across pure conversion steps (4,650.00 at steps 1 and 2) and only moves on genuine variance, which is precisely the anti-double-count invariant worth testing.

results.what_source_actually_says: 'For Purchasing orders, the commitment reduction, and as consequence, the consumption confirmation, is processed based on the related documents posted against the purchasing document like goods receipt (GR), invoices (IV), credit memo (CM), etc.'
results.notes: Tier 2 (SAP-hosted support wiki, 'Additional Content'), behavioural claim, so CONFIRMED is permitted. Mechanism detail: relief is computed from the PO history table EKBE, debit documents SHKZG='S', credit documents SHKZG='H'.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full passage: 'If in PO, the goods receipt flag is set, it means that incoming goods are expected. The flag \'goods unvalued\' available on the PO document, controls whether the commitment is decreased when goods are received or when an invoice has been posted. When the indicator "goods receipt non-valuated" is set, it means that the information from IV will be used to reduce the commitments created for the PO.' Section 6 names the field: EKBP-WEUNB. GR fields (WEMNG/WEWTW/WEWHW) drive relief when GR is valuated; invoice fields (REMNG/REWTW/REWHW) drive relief when GR is non-valuated.
results.notes: THE DECISIVE RECORD FOR THE TASK. This is the only source in the lane that states the two-gate mechanism explicitly and names the controlling field. It is Tier 2. See contradictions[0] - the blueprint should not rest the GR-vs-IR switch on the Tier-1 GR-indicator sentence alone.

results.replacement_quote: When the actual goods receipt for the purchase order is posted, the forecast material purchasing costs/the simulated postings are reversed in the enhancement ledger and the actual documents for the goods receipt/material costs are posted in the leading ledger. The value on the GR/IR account in the extension ledger is also reversed.
results.what_source_actually_says: The recorded evidence_quote is NOT a contiguous string on the page: it silently elides '/the simulated postings' from the middle of the sentence. The claim itself is correct and the corrected full sentence is supplied as replacement_quote. A second, independent restatement of the same mechanism appears later on the page: 'When the goods receipt is saved, the forecast material purchasing costs are reversed in the extension ledger and posted as actual material costs in the leading ledger 0L. The amount on the GR/IR account is also reversed in the extension ledger.'
results.notes: QUOTE DEFECT ONLY - substance stands. This is the S/4HANA-new-model expression of the anti-double-count invariant: the forecast is REVERSED in the extension ledger at the same moment the actual is posted in the leading ledger, so summing the two ledgers never double-counts. Replace the quote in the blueprint.

results.what_source_actually_says: Verbatim, first bullet of an explicitly 'complete list of all restrictions'. Other restrictions on the same list that bear directly on this engagement: 'No manual commitments are supported'; 'No commitment carry forward is supported'; 'Only purchase orders and purchase requisitions are supported'; 'No separate commitments for freight costs are possible'; 'Commitments from down payments are not supported'; 'A GR/IR account needs to be configured'; 'Purchase order or purchase requisition with account assignment G/L account of cost element category 90 is not supported... Therefore, an account assignment WBS element in combination with asset is not supported'; max 499 account assignments per PO (249 if referencing a PR).
results.notes: HIGH VALUE, UNDER-CAPTURED BY THE LANE. Four of these restrictions directly contradict capabilities the lane records elsewhere for CLASSIC commitment management: freight commitments (R04-019/036), down-payment commitment interaction (R04-071), commitment carry-forward (R04-109/110/111), and the WBS-plus-asset assignment implied by the Investment Management down-payment records (R04-083..087). None of those contradictions are errors - they are classic-vs-new scope differences - but the blueprint MUST state which commitment model it is targeting or it will specify a system that cannot exist.

results.what_source_actually_says: Full sentence: 'If the goods receipt was non-valuated or no delivery was expected, the supplier invoice reduces the commitment of the purchase order. In this case, it is possible to change the proposed account assignments for the purchase order in the supplier invoice.' The PO-side summary on the same page states the whole rule in one line: 'Purchase orders and the correspondent budget consumption are reduced either by a valuated goods receipt or by supplier invoices if the goods receipt is non-valuated, or delivery is not expected.'
results.notes: THE CLEANEST SINGLE STATEMENT OF THE ANSWER TO THE TASK QUESTION. Two branch conditions, not one: (a) GR non-valuated, or (b) no delivery expected (GR indicator not set). Triangulates exactly with Tier-1 R04-121 (branch b) and Tier-2 R04-038 (branch a). Same PSM scope caveat as R04-068.

results.what_source_actually_says: Verbatim, plus 'The account assignments from the purchase orders cannot be changed in this case' and 'In case of price and quantity difference between the invoice and goods receipts, additional postings are generated using the GR/IR clearing program.'
results.notes: This is the no-double-count guarantee on the valuated route: after a valuated GR the invoice is a VARIANCE-ONLY event. Independently demonstrated by the Tier-1 numeric table at 337cd..., where the over-priced invoice moves Assigned by exactly the variance. PSM scope caveat applies.

results.what_source_actually_says: Verbatim, plus the reversal rule the claim omits: 'This specific reduction is reversed whenever the down payment is cleared.'
results.notes: The omitted second sentence matters for anti-double-counting: the down-payment reduction is TEMPORARY and unwinds on clearing, so a naive implementation that permanently relieves commitment on down payment will under-state commitment after clearing. The claim is PSM-scoped by its own vocabulary ('budget consumption amount type'), so no downgrade. Note the S/4HANA new commitment model does NOT support down-payment commitments at all (R04-066).

results.what_source_actually_says: Verbatim. The same page gives the quantity-first rule and a worked example that the lane did not capture: 'During commitment updating, purchase orders and purchase requisitions are reduced-quantity based. This means that the open amount is calculated by considering the open quantity first. This mechanism avoids open amounts in the case of price decreases... Purchase requisition: 10 x $10 = $100 (open commitment). Reduced by purchase order (lower price): 10 x $9 = $90 (open commitment). In this case, the purchase requisition is completely reduced because there are no quantities open to be ordered.'
results.notes: HIGH VALUE ADDITION. This worked example closes the exact failure mode a value-based PR relief would create: ordering the FULL quantity at a LOWER price must still zero the PR commitment, leaving no $10 phantom residual. It is the price-decrease mirror of the Tier-1 price-increase example in R04-011. Recommend capturing as a first-class test scenario.

results.what_source_actually_says: Verbatim, opening sentence of Use. Deliverable 'Invoicing', 2025 FPS01.

contradictions.headline: The GR-versus-IR switch is TWO gates, not one. Every individual claim is confirmed, but the Tier-1 rule the blueprint would naturally quote is not the whole rule.
contradictions.detail: Tier-1 SAP PS documentation ('Reducing Purchase Order Commitments to Zero', re-fetched 2026-08-05) states flatly: 'The goods receipt indicator in the purchase order determines when the commitment is reduced and actual costs are set up... GR indicator set: Commitment is reduced when goods are received. GR Indicator is not set: Commitment is reduced when invoices are received.' Read alone, that is a single-field rule. Two other re-fetched sources show a SECOND, independent gate. The SAP support wiki 'Commitments in Purchasing' says: 'If in PO, the goods receipt flag is set, it means that incoming goods are expected. The flag \'goods unvalued\' available on the PO document, controls whether the commitment is decreased when goods are received or when an invoice has been posted. When the indicator "goods receipt non-valuated" is set, it means that the information from IV will be used to reduce the commitments created for the PO.' It names the field (EKBP-WEUNB) and the two field sets that drive relief (WEMNG/WEWTW/WEWHW for valuated GR, REMNG/REWTW/REWHW for non-valuated). The S/4HANA Cloud PSM lesson states the combined rule in one line: 'Purchase orders and the correspondent budget consumption are reduced either by a valuated goods receipt or by supplier invoices if the goods receipt is non-valuated, or delivery is not expected.'
contradictions.resolved_rule: Commitment relief on a PO item resolves in this order: (1) GR indicator NOT set (no delivery expected) -> the INVOICE relieves. (2) GR indicator set AND goods receipt VALUATED -> the GOODS RECEIPT relieves, and the later invoice moves the number only by price/quantity variance. (3) GR indicator set AND goods receipt NON-VALUATED -> the INVOICE relieves; the GR has no financial impact. Route (3) is the one a single-field implementation gets wrong, because the GR indicator IS set yet the goods receipt must not relieve.
contradictions.answer_to_task_question: Reduction is NEITHER unconditionally at GR NOR unconditionally at IR - it is CONFIGURABLE, per purchase order item, via two fields: the goods receipt indicator (is a delivery expected at all) and the goods-receipt-non-valuated flag (is that delivery financially relevant). Account assignment category is the upstream driver of the valuation flag - Tier-2 learning.sap.com: 'Based on the account assignment category of the purchase order, actual costs are posted upon goods receipt or invoice receipt (valuated, non-valuated goods receipt)', and 'For account assignment category F, the good receipt is valuated.'
contradictions.evidence_tier_warning: The decisive second gate rests on Tier-2 sources only. The Tier-1 PS page states the single-field version. If the blueprint needs a Tier-1 citation for the valuation gate specifically, it does not currently have one, and the spmm wiki points to SAP Notes 355793 / 639523 / 670489, none of which were retrievable in this run.
contradictions.design_consequence: An anti-double-counting design that keys relief solely on the GR indicator will, for non-valuated-GR purchase orders, relieve commitment at goods receipt while actual cost only arrives at invoice - opening a window in which the item is counted in NEITHER actual nor commitment, understating Assigned. The symmetric error (relieving at both GR and IR) double-relieves. Model the pair of fields, not one.

contradictions.headline: The worked GR/IR example numbers in R04-033 do not match the SAP table they cite.
contradictions.detail: R04-033 asserts the invoice 'raises both actual and assigned totals from 4650.00 to 6150.00'. The re-fetched table shows Actual moving 3,100.00 -> 4,100.00 at the invoice step, and only reaching 6,150.00 at step 4 (the final goods receipt). Only ASSIGNED moves 4,650.00 -> 6,150.00 at the invoice step. Two facts visible in the table and captured by no record: the invoice for three PC posted when only two PC had been received INCREASES commitment 1,550.00 -> 2,050.00 (a revaluation, not a relief); and Assigned stays flat at 4,650.00 across the pure GR conversion step, moving only on genuine price variance.
contradictions.design_consequence: Downgraded to OVERSTATED. Do not seed test scenarios from this claim as written. The flat-Assigned-across-conversion property is the actual invariant worth asserting in tests.

contradictions.headline: Several confirmed capabilities of CLASSIC commitment management are explicitly unsupported in the NEW S/4HANA commitment management, and the lane does not mark which model each record describes.
contradictions.detail: The re-fetched 'complete list of all restrictions' for the new (ACDOCA extension-ledger) solution includes: 'No separate commitments for freight costs are possible' (versus R04-019/036, which commit freight and manage it separately); 'Commitments from down payments are not supported' (versus R04-071); 'No commitment carry forward is supported' (versus R04-109/110/111); 'Commitment Overhead Calculation is not supported' (versus R04-107); 'The correction report RKANBU01... can not be used to correct new commitment (table ACDOCA)! There\'s no report which automatically adjusts or corrects new commitment in ACDOCA' (versus R04-050); 'No manual commitments are supported'; 'Only purchase orders and purchase requisitions are supported'; and an account-assignment WBS-element-plus-asset combination is not supported.
contradictions.design_consequence: These are not errors in the lane - they are two different SAP mechanisms. But the blueprint must declare which commitment model the source SAP-WBS system runs, or it will specify a target that mirrors capabilities the source does not have. Note also that both models post in parallel (COOI and ACDOCA), so a reconciliation design must nominate one as authoritative.

additional_findings_not_in_lane: PRICE-DECREASE CASE (missing test scenario): the PSM lesson gives the mirror of the Tier-1 price-increase example - 'Purchase requisition: 10 x $10 = $100 (open commitment). Reduced by purchase order (lower price): 10 x $9 = $90... the purchase requisition is completely reduced because there are no quantities open to be ordered.' Quantity-first relief is what prevents a $10 phantom PR residual. Pair with R04-011 as the two canonical PR-relief tests.

IDEMPOTENT FULL-RESTATEMENT INTERFACE (R04-120): SAP sends the complete current picture on every event, not deltas, and lets the receiving side recompute open = purchased - reduced. This is the single most transferable anti-double-count pattern in the lane and deserves to be a design principle rather than a buried data-model note.

GR VERSUS INVOICE ASYMMETRY ON MULTI-ACCOUNT ITEMS (R04-118 source text): goods receipts distribute across multiple account assignments progressive-fill-up ONLY (EKBE ZEKKN = '0'), whereas invoices offer both progressive and proportional via EKPO-TWRKZ. A design offering a single distribution mode for both will diverge from SAP on one of them.

DOWN-PAYMENT RELIEF IS REVERSIBLE (R04-071 source text, omitted from the claim): 'This specific reduction is reversed whenever the down payment is cleared.' A permanent commitment relief on down payment under-states commitment after clearing.

UNPLANNED DELIVERY COSTS POSTED TO A SEPARATE G/L ACCOUNT ARE INVISIBLE IN PO HISTORY (R04-075 source text): 'The system does not display unplanned delivery costs that were posted to a separate G/L account in the purchase order history.' Relevant to any reconciliation that walks PO history to rebuild landed cost.

COMMITMENT ACTIVATION HAS A SECOND PER-OBJECT GATE (R04-117 source text): controlling-area activation via OKKP is necessary but not sufficient - orders need the order-type switch, cost centres need the lock indicator clear, projects are covered by note 47992, and per-item relevance is flagged by XOBLR on EBAN/EKPO.
SERVICE INVOICE OVERRUN IS A WARNING, NOT A BLOCK (R04-092 source text): 'the system issues a warning message'. Do not design a hard stop where SAP advises.
gaps_reconfirmed: RETENTION vs COMMITMENT remains genuinely unknown. I re-read the full Retention topic; it says nothing about whether retention affects the PO commitment balance. The lane's gap note is correct and must not be quietly resolved.

PR/PO COMMITMENT VALUE TYPE CODES remain unsourced. R04-053 confirms only that the two value types DIFFER. Value type 11 (statistical actual) is the only code any source in this lane prints. Do not hard-code commitment value type numbers.

SERVICE ENTRY SHEET ACCEPTANCE -> commitment reduction remains an inference. No re-fetched page states the causal link in one sentence. The PSM lesson comes closest - 'Service entry sheets update the budget consumption using their corresponding goods receipts once they are approved' - which routes service relief through a generated goods receipt rather than through acceptance directly. That is a useful narrowing but still not the claimed sentence.

PO AMENDMENT RECALCULATION remains undesigned. R04-119 confirms a change-detection routine exists but no source enumerates which fields are commitment-relevant or how a mid-receipt quantity/price change recalculates. Must be designed, not copied.
PROJECT-LEVEL COMMITMENT CARRY-FORWARD (CJCF) was again not reachable. Carry-forward is evidenced for cost centres (KSCF, Tier-1) and sales orders (Tier-1, and now correctly narrowed - see R04-111).
STOCK TRANSFER INTO PROJECT STOCK remains indirect only - a BAdI name plus special stock indicator Q. No page describes commitment behaviour for an intra-company stock transfer into project stock.

summary.quote_match_rate: 122/123 exact or substantively exact; 1 quote (R04-065) was a non-contiguous elision and has been replaced
summary.verdict_on_lane_quality: High. Every one of the 24 source URLs re-rendered, every rendered title matched the intended topic, and 122 of 123 evidence quotes were found verbatim in independently re-fetched text - including SAP's own typos ('Plannend', 'the good receipt'), stray spaces and curly quotes, which is strong evidence the lane transcribed rather than paraphrased. No claim was contradicted. The four downgrades are a dropped precondition (R04-031), a misread numeric table (R04-033), an unstated default (R04-051), and a product-scope generalisation (R04-111). The lane's own gaps section is honest and I re-confirmed all six of its material gaps rather than closing any of them.
summary.residual_risk: The lane's principal weakness is not falsity but INCOMPLETENESS on the exact question this verification targeted. The GR-versus-IR switch is recorded as a single-field rule from Tier-1 and as a two-field rule from Tier-2, and nothing in the lane reconciles them. The second gate - the goods-receipt-non-valuated flag - is load-bearing for the anti-double-counting design and currently rests on Tier-2 evidence only.
